subproblem.title: Density limit from monotonicity of the exponentially weighted ratio
subproblem.statement: Let P : ℝ → [0,∞] and ρ0, Λ ∈ ℝ with ρ0 > 0. Assume that the function ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ})·P(ρ) is monotone non-decreasing on the open interval (0, ρ0), and that P(ρ0/2) ≠ ∞. Then there is θ ∈ [0,∞] such that P(t) → θ as t → 0 with t > 0 (along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of ℝ, in the order topology of [0,∞]), θ ≠ ∞, and θ ≤ ofReal(e^{Λσ})·P(σ) for every σ with 0 < σ < ρ0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (ρ₀ Λ : ℝ), 0 < ρ₀ → MonotoneOn (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * ρ)) * P ρ) (Ioo 0 ρ₀) → P (ρ₀ / 2) ≠ ∞ → ∃ θ : ℝ≥0∞, Tendsto P (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 θ) ∧ θ ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ → σ < ρ₀ → θ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * σ)) * P σ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 8 of the parent node's supplied proof of Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 8, 3.3 (printed p. 210): existence and finiteness of Θⁿ(μ_V, x) and the bound Θ ≤ e^{Λσ}ω_n^{-1}σ^{-n}μ_V(B_σ(x)) follow from monotonicity of e^{Λρ}ω_n^{-1}ρ^{-n}μ_V(B_ρ(x)) on (0, ρ0) and e^{Λρ} → 1 as ρ ↓ 0. It is stated here abstractly for a [0,∞]-valued function P; in the parent it is applied with P = densityRatio n μ_V x (so the conclusion Tendsto P (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 θ) is HasDensity n μ_V x θ by definition). Only the order topologies of ℝ and [0,∞] and continuity of multiplication on [0,∞] away from (0,∞),(∞,0) are used.

Notation. For ρ ∈ ℝ put h(ρ) := ofReal(e^{Λρ})·P(ρ) ∈ [0,∞]; I := (0, ρ0) = Ioo 0 ρ0; "t → 0+" means along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of ℝ.

Proof. Fix P : ℝ → [0,∞] and ρ0, Λ ∈ ℝ with (H1) ρ0 > 0; (H2) h is monotone (non-decreasing) on I; (H3) P(ρ0/2) ≠ ∞.

1. Definition of θ. I is nonempty (ρ0/2 ∈ I by (H1)) and h(I) ⊆ [0,∞] is bounded below by 0. Put θ := inf h(I) ∈ [0,∞].

2. h(t) → θ as t → 0+. This is MonotoneOn.tendsto_nhdsWithin_Ioo_right applied to h on I = (0, ρ0); directly: in the order topology of [0,∞] it suffices that (a) for every a < θ, h(t) > a for all t in a set of 𝓝[>] 0, and (b) for every b > θ, h(t) < b for all t in a set of 𝓝[>] 0. For (a) take I itself, which belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 since ρ0 > 0: for t ∈ I, h(t) ≥ θ > a. For (b), b > θ = inf h(I) gives s ∈ I with h(s) < b; every t ∈ (0, s) lies in I with t ≤ s, so h(t) ≤ h(s) < b by (H2); and (0, s) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0.

3. Lower bound. For every σ with 0 < σ < ρ0, σ ∈ I, so θ = inf h(I) ≤ h(σ) = ofReal(e^{Λσ})·P(σ). This is the third conclusion.

4. Finiteness. By 3 with σ = ρ0/2 (0 < ρ0/2 < ρ0 by (H1)), θ ≤ ofReal(e^{Λρ0/2})·P(ρ0/2); the first factor is finite (ofReal of a real number) and the second is finite by (H3), so their product is finite and θ ≠ ∞.

5. Removing the weight. For every t ∈ ℝ, since e^{−Λt} ≥ 0, ofReal(e^{−Λt})·h(t) = (ofReal(e^{−Λt})·ofReal(e^{Λt}))·P(t) = ofReal(e^{−Λt}·e^{Λt})·P(t) = ofReal(e^{0})·P(t) = ofReal(1)·P(t) = P(t).

6. The function t ↦ ofReal(e^{−Λt}) from ℝ to [0,∞] is continuous (composition of continuous maps), with value ofReal(1) = 1 at t = 0; hence it tends to 1 as t → 0 and a fortiori as t → 0+ (𝓝[>] 0 ≤ 𝓝 0).

7. Multiplication [0,∞] × [0,∞] → [0,∞] is continuous at (1, θ) because 1 ≠ 0 and 1 ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.Tendsto.mul, whose side conditions are "1 ≠ 0 or θ ≠ ∞" and "θ ≠ 0 or 1 ≠ ∞"). By 2 and 6, ofReal(e^{−Λt})·h(t) → 1·θ = θ as t → 0+, and by 5 the left side equals P(t) for every t. Hence P(t) → θ as t → 0+.

8. Conclusion. θ witnesses the statement: P → θ along 𝓝[>] 0 (step 7), θ ≠ ∞ (step 4), and θ ≤ ofReal(e^{Λσ})·P(σ) for all 0 < σ < ρ0 (step 3). As P, ρ0, Λ were arbitrary, the statement holds.
proof_key_steps: θ := inf of h(ρ) = ofReal(e^{Λρ})·P(ρ) over (0, ρ0); the monotone h tends to θ at 0+ (MonotoneOn.tendsto_nhdsWithin_Ioo_right).
θ ≤ h(σ) for 0 < σ < ρ0; in particular θ ≤ h(ρ0/2) < ∞.
P(t) = ofReal(e^{−Λt})·h(t) for all t, and ofReal(e^{−Λt}) → 1 as t → 0+.
ENNReal.Tendsto.mul at (1, θ) (1 ≠ 0, 1 ≠ ∞) gives P(t) → θ.

subproblem.title: Integrating-factor comparison (mean value theorem form)
subproblem.statement: Let L, a, b ∈ ℝ and f, g, f', g' : ℝ → ℝ with L ≥ 0, a ≥ 0 and a ≤ b. Assume that for every t in the closed interval [a, b]: f has derivative f'(t) at t, g has derivative g'(t) at t, 0 ≤ f'(t) + L·f(t), and g'(t) ≤ f'(t) + L·f(t). Then e^{L·a}·f(a) + (g(b) − g(a)) ≤ e^{L·b}·f(b).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (L a b : ℝ) (f g f' g' : ℝ → ℝ), 0 ≤ L → 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, HasDerivAt f (f' t) t) → (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, HasDerivAt g (g' t) t) → (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, 0 ≤ f' t + L * f t) → (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, g' t ≤ f' t + L * f t) → Real.exp (L * a) * f a + (g b - g a) ≤ Real.exp (L * b) * f b
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4 (4.1 and 4.3) of the parent node's supplied proof of Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 8, 3.3 (printed p. 210, "Cf. 4.7 of Ch. 4"; the integrating-factor argument of Ch. 4, 3.15–3.17, printed pp. 92–93): multiplying the differential inequality for f = I/tⁿ by the integrating factor e^{Lt} and integrating from a to b by the mean value theorem. It is stated here for arbitrary real functions. In the parent it is applied, for each small ε > 0, on [a, b] = [σ, ρ] with L = (1 + ε)Λ, f(t) = I_ε(t)/tⁿ (I_ε = SimonGMT's cutoffMass x (monotonicityCutoff ε)), f'(t) = J'_ε(t)/tⁿ − δV(X_t)/t^{n+1} (SimonGMT's hasDerivAt_normalized_weightedCutoffMass with h ≡ 1), g = G_ε (the truncated-defect cutoff integral) and g' = G'_ε.

Implementation note: this node is expected to be a leaf: a single declaration Submission.mono833_integrating_factor_comparison using only the frozen contract's imports. A scratch proof of exactly this shape compiled with only `import GMT.Ch08.Submission` (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and passed the leaf-delta check, using HasDerivAt.const_mul and HasDerivAt.exp on (hasDerivAt_id t), HasDerivAt.mul, HasDerivAt.fun_sub (the pointwise-difference form, so that HasDerivAt.deriv rewrites `deriv (fun s ↦ e^{Ls} f s − g s) t`), monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg on convex_Icc, interior_subset, Real.one_le_exp and nlinarith.

Proof. Fix L, a, b ∈ ℝ and f, g, f', g' : ℝ → ℝ with: (H1) L ≥ 0; (H2) a ≥ 0; (H3) a ≤ b; (H4) for every t ∈ [a, b], f has derivative f'(t) at t; (H5) for every t ∈ [a, b], g has derivative g'(t) at t; (H6) 0 ≤ f'(t) + L·f(t) for every t ∈ [a, b]; (H7) g'(t) ≤ f'(t) + L·f(t) for every t ∈ [a, b]. We show e^{La}·f(a) + (g(b) − g(a)) ≤ e^{Lb}·f(b).

1. Let F(s) := e^{Ls}·f(s). For t ∈ [a, b], s ↦ e^{Ls} has derivative L·e^{Lt} at t (chain rule), so by (H4) and the product rule F has derivative F'(t) = L·e^{Lt}·f(t) + e^{Lt}·f'(t) = e^{Lt}·(f'(t) + L·f(t)) at t.

2. Let H(s) := F(s) − g(s). By 1 and (H5), for every t ∈ [a, b], H has derivative H'(t) = e^{Lt}·(f'(t) + L·f(t)) − g'(t) at t. In particular H is continuous at every point of [a, b] (hence continuous on [a, b]) and differentiable at every point of the open interval (a, b), with deriv H(t) = H'(t) there.

3. H' ≥ 0 on (a, b). Let t ∈ (a, b) ⊆ [a, b]. Then t ≥ a ≥ 0 and L ≥ 0, so L·t ≥ 0 and e^{Lt} ≥ 1. Put u := f'(t) + L·f(t); u ≥ 0 by (H6). Hence e^{Lt}·u ≥ u (as (e^{Lt} − 1)·u ≥ 0) and u ≥ g'(t) by (H7), so H'(t) = e^{Lt}·u − g'(t) ≥ 0.

4. By the mean value theorem in the form "a function continuous on the convex set [a, b], differentiable on its interior (a, b) with nonnegative derivative there, is monotone on [a, b]" (monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg; interior [a, b] = (a, b)), H is non-decreasing on [a, b]. Since a, b ∈ [a, b] and a ≤ b (H3), H(a) ≤ H(b), i.e.
   e^{La}·f(a) − g(a) ≤ e^{Lb}·f(b) − g(b).

5. Adding g(b) to both sides gives e^{La}·f(a) + (g(b) − g(a)) ≤ e^{Lb}·f(b), the claim. As L, a, b, f, g, f', g' were arbitrary, the statement holds.

H = F − g has derivative e^{Lt}·(f' + L·f) − g' on [a, b], so H is continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b).
On (a, b): L·t ≥ 0 gives e^{Lt} ≥ 1, and f' + L·f is both ≥ 0 and ≥ g', so H' ≥ 0.
Mean value theorem (monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg on the convex set [a, b]) gives H(a) ≤ H(b), which rearranges to the claim.

subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let ν and μ be measures on ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), let x ∈ ℝ^N, ρ0, Λ, A, t ∈ ℝ and φ : ℝ → ℝ. Assume: ν(B_r(x)) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ(B_r(x)) for every r with 0 < r < ρ0, where B_r(x) = closedBall x r; φ is continuous; φ is antitone (non-increasing); φ(s) = 1 for every s ≤ 1; φ(s) = 0 for every s ≥ A²; A > 0; t > 0; t·A < ρ0. Then ∫⁻ ofReal(φ(|y − x|²/t²)) dν(y) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·∫⁻ ofReal(φ(|y − x|²/t²)) dμ(y), the integrals being lower Lebesgue integrals with values in [0,∞].

It is used inside the sibling node Submission.mono833_radial_first_variation_bound with ν = V.firstVariationRieszMeasure hV (= variationMeasure V = ‖δV‖) and μ = μ_V = V.weight, and, through that node, in the parent with φ = SimonGMT's monotonicityCutoff ε and A = 1 + ε. No finiteness of ν or μ and no sign condition on Λ is needed (ofReal(Λ) = 0 when Λ < 0).

Notation. B_r := closedBall x r (Euclidean closed ball), |·| the Euclidean norm, c(y) := φ(|y − x|²/t²) for y ∈ ℝ^N. All integrals are lower Lebesgue integrals ∫⁻ of [0,∞]-valued functions.

Implementation note: this node is expected to be a leaf, i.e. a single declaration Submission.mono833_radial_layer_cake_le using only the frozen contract's imports (no new import, helper declaration or set_option). A scratch proof of exactly this shape compiled with only `import GMT.Ch08.Submission` (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and passed the workflow's leaf-delta check; it used MeasureTheory.lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le, lintegral_const_mul', setLIntegral_mono' with measurableSet_Ioi, IsClosed.csSup_mem, le_csSup, isClosed_le, Real.sqrt_lt', Real.sq_sqrt, pow_le_pow_iff_left₀ and pow_le_pow_left₀ (in this Mathlib, Set.mem_setOf_eq is deprecated; Set.mem_ofPred_eq is its warning-free replacement).

Proof. Fix N, ν, μ, x, ρ0, Λ, A, t, φ and assume the hypotheses: (H1) ν(B_r) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ(B_r) whenever 0 < r < ρ0; (H2) φ is continuous; (H3) φ is antitone (s ≤ s' ⇒ φ(s') ≤ φ(s)); (H4) φ(s) = 1 for every s ≤ 1; (H5) φ(s) = 0 for every s ≥ A²; (H6) A > 0; (H7) t > 0; (H8) t·A < ρ0.

1. 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1. Let s ∈ ℝ. Since s ≤ max(s, A²), (H3) and (H5) give φ(s) ≥ φ(max(s, A²)) = 0. Since min(s, 1) ≤ s, (H3) and (H4) give φ(s) ≤ φ(min(s, 1)) = 1.

2. The function c(y) = φ(|y − x|²/t²) is continuous on ℝ^N (a composition of the continuous maps y ↦ y − x, the norm, squaring, division by the constant t², and φ by (H2)); hence it is Borel measurable, and by 1, 0 ≤ c(y) ≤ 1 for every y.

3. Layer-cake formula. For any measure m on ℝ^N and any measurable g ≥ 0, ∫⁻ ofReal(g) dm = ∫⁻_{s ∈ (0,∞)} m({y : s ≤ g(y)}) ds (Mathlib lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le; it needs only g ≥ 0 a.e. and a.e.-measurability, no finiteness of m). By 2 it applies to g = c with m = ν and with m = μ:
   ∫⁻ ofReal(c) dν = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ν({c ≥ s}) ds,   ∫⁻ ofReal(c) dμ = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ({c ≥ s}) ds,
   where {c ≥ s} := {y : s ≤ c(y)}.

4. Claim: for every s > 0, ν({c ≥ s}) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ({c ≥ s}).
   4a. If s > 1, then c(y) ≤ 1 < s for all y (by 2), so {c ≥ s} = ∅ and both sides equal 0.
   4b. Let 0 < s ≤ 1 and E := {τ ∈ ℝ : s ≤ φ(τ)}. E is closed, being the preimage of [s, ∞) under the continuous φ. 1 ∈ E, because φ(1) = 1 ≥ s by (H4). E is bounded above by A²: if τ ∈ E had τ > A², then φ(τ) = 0 < s by (H5), contradicting τ ∈ E. Hence b := sup E is a real number, and b ∈ E because E is closed, nonempty and bounded above. Since 1 ∈ E, b ≥ 1. Moreover b < A²: otherwise φ(b) = 0 < s by (H5), contradicting b ∈ E.
   4c. E = (−∞, b]. Indeed, every τ ∈ E satisfies τ ≤ sup E = b; conversely, if τ ≤ b then φ(τ) ≥ φ(b) ≥ s by (H3) and b ∈ E, so τ ∈ E.
   4d. Put r := t·√b. Then for y ∈ ℝ^N: y ∈ {c ≥ s} ⟺ |y − x|²/t² ≤ b (by 4c) ⟺ |y − x|² ≤ b·t² = r² (t² > 0, and r² = t²·b since b ≥ 0) ⟺ |y − x| ≤ r (both |y − x| and r are ≥ 0, and squaring is strictly increasing on [0, ∞)) ⟺ y ∈ B_r. So {c ≥ s} = B_r.
   4e. r > 0 since t > 0 and b ≥ 1 > 0. And r < ρ0: since 0 ≤ b < A² and A > 0, √b < A (Real.sqrt_lt'), so r = t√b < tA < ρ0 by (H7) and (H8).
   4f. By (H1) with this r, ν({c ≥ s}) = ν(B_r) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ(B_r) = ofReal(Λ)·μ({c ≥ s}).

5. Conclusion. By 3, 4 and monotonicity of the lower integral over the measurable set (0, ∞) (pointwise inequality on (0,∞), setLIntegral_mono'), and then pulling the constant ofReal(Λ) ≠ ∞ out of the lower integral (lintegral_const_mul', which needs no measurability):
   ∫⁻ ofReal(c) dν = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ν({c ≥ s}) ds ≤ ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} ofReal(Λ)·μ({c ≥ s}) ds = ofReal(Λ)·∫⁻_{(0,∞)} μ({c ≥ s}) ds = ofReal(Λ)·∫⁻ ofReal(c) dμ.
   Since c(y) = φ(|y − x|²/t²), this is exactly the asserted inequality ∫⁻ ofReal(φ(|y − x|²/t²)) dν(y) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·∫⁻ ofReal(φ(|y − x|²/t²)) dμ(y). As N, ν, μ, x, ρ0, Λ, A, t, φ were arbitrary, the statement holds.
proof_key_steps: Antitonicity with φ = 1 on (−∞,1] and φ = 0 on [A²,∞) gives 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1; c(y) = φ(|y − x|²/t²) is continuous, hence measurable, with 0 ≤ c ≤ 1.
Layer cake (lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_le) for ν and for μ: ∫⁻ ofReal(c) dm = ∫⁻_{(0,∞)} m({c ≥ s}) ds.
For s > 1, {c ≥ s} = ∅. For 0 < s ≤ 1, E = {τ : s ≤ φ(τ)} is closed, contains 1 and is bounded above by A², so b = sup E ∈ E, 1 ≤ b < A², and E = (−∞, b] by antitonicity.
Hence {c ≥ s} = closedBall x (t√b) with 0 < t√b < tA < ρ0, and the ball hypothesis gives ν({c ≥ s}) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ({c ≥ s}) for every s > 0.
Integrate over (0,∞) (setLIntegral_mono') and pull out ofReal(Λ) ≠ ∞ (lintegral_const_mul').

Proof. Fix N, n, U, V, x, ρ0, Λ, A, t, φ and assume: (H0) V has locally bounded first variation in U; (H1) ball x ρ0 ⊆ U; (H2) Λ ≥ 0; (H3) ‖δV‖(B_r) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ_V(B_r) for 0 < r < ρ0; (H4) φ is C¹; (H5) φ is antitone; (H6) φ(s) = 1 for s ≤ 1; (H7) φ(s) = 0 for s ≥ A²; (H8) A > 0; (H9) t > 0; (H10) t·A < ρ0. We must show |δV(X)| ≤ A·Λ·t·∫ c dμ_V.

1. 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1: for s ∈ ℝ, (H5) and (H7) give φ(s) ≥ φ(max(s, A²)) = 0, and (H5) and (H6) give φ(s) ≤ φ(min(s, 1)) = 1. The function c is continuous on ℝ^N (φ is continuous by (H4)), hence measurable, and 0 ≤ c ≤ 1.

2. Support of c. If c(y) ≠ 0 then |y − x| < tA. Indeed, if |y − x| ≥ tA (> 0 by (H8), (H9)), then |y − x|² ≥ (tA)² = A²t², so |y − x|²/t² ≥ A² and c(y) = 0 by (H7).

3. Pointwise bound. For every y, |X(y)| = c(y)·|y − x| ≤ tA·c(y): if c(y) = 0 both sides vanish; otherwise |y − x| < tA by 2 and c(y) ≥ 0.

4. X is a test field. X is C¹ on ℝ^N: y ↦ |y − x|² is smooth (contDiff_norm_sq composed with y ↦ y − x), division by the constant t² and composition with the C¹ map φ keep it C¹, and the product of the C¹ scalar c with the smooth field y ↦ y − x is C¹. Every y with X(y) ≠ 0 has c(y) ≠ 0, hence |y − x| < tA by 2, hence y ∈ B_{tA}; since B_{tA} is closed, tsupport X = closure{X ≠ 0} ⊆ B_{tA}. B_{tA} is compact, so tsupport X is compact (a closed subset of a compact set), i.e. X has compact support. Finally B_{tA} ⊆ ball x ρ0 ⊆ U because tA < ρ0 (H10) and (H1). Thus X defines an element of K(U; ℝ^N), i.e. a Varifold.TestVectorField U whose underlying function is X.

5. Polar representation (Simon Ch. 8, 2.6). By the definition of variationMeasure and (H0) (dif_pos), ‖δV‖ = m.

6. Finiteness. 0 < tA < ρ0, so by (H3) and 5, m(B_{tA}) = ‖δV‖(B_{tA}) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ_V(B_{tA}); and μ_V(B_{tA}) < ∞ because B_{tA} is a compact subset of U (step 4; Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact). Hence m(B_{tA}) < ∞ and μ_V(B_{tA}) < ∞.

7. Integrability of c. Let m' be a measure on ℝ^N with m'(B_{tA}) < ∞. Then c is m'-integrable: c is continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable; |c| ≤ 1 on the finite-measure set B_{tA}, so c is integrable on B_{tA}; and c vanishes outside B_{tA} by 2. By 6 this applies to m' = m and to m' = μ_V.

8. First estimate. Applying 5 to Y = X and using 3:
   |δV(X)| = |∫⟨η, X⟩ dm| ≤ ∫|⟨η, X⟩| dm ≤ ∫ tA·c dm = tA·∫ c dm.
   The second inequality is monotonicity of the integral of integrable functions (|⟨η, X⟩| is integrable by 5, tA·c by 7) under the m-a.e. bound |⟨η(y), X(y)⟩| ≤ |η(y)|·|X(y)| = |X(y)| ≤ tA·c(y) (Cauchy–Schwarz, |η| = 1 m-a.e., and 3).

9. Layer-cake comparison (sibling lemma). The hypotheses of Submission.mono833_radial_layer_cake_le hold with (ν, μ) := (m, μ_V) and the same x, ρ0, Λ, A, t, φ: for 0 < r < ρ0, m(B_r) = ‖δV‖(B_r) ≤ ofReal(Λ)·μ_V(B_r) by 5 and (H3); φ is continuous (H4), antitone (H5), satisfies (H6) and (H7); A > 0, t > 0, tA < ρ0. Hence ∫⁻ ofReal(c) dm ≤ ofReal(Λ)·∫⁻ ofReal(c) dμ_V.

10. Back to real integrals. Since c ≥ 0 is measurable, ∫ c dm = (∫⁻ ofReal(c) dm).toReal and ∫ c dμ_V = (∫⁻ ofReal(c) dμ_V).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae). The quantity ∫⁻ ofReal(c) dμ_V is finite because c is μ_V-integrable (7), so ofReal(Λ)·∫⁻ ofReal(c) dμ_V is finite, and toReal is monotone on [0,∞) for a finite upper bound. Therefore, using toReal(ofReal(Λ)·a) = Λ·toReal(a) for Λ ≥ 0 (H2):
   ∫ c dm ≤ (ofReal(Λ)·∫⁻ ofReal(c) dμ_V).toReal = Λ·∫ c dμ_V.

11. Conclusion. Since tA ≥ 0, steps 8 and 10 give
   |δV(X)| ≤ tA·∫ c dm ≤ tA·Λ·∫ c dμ_V = A·Λ·t·∫ c dμ_V,
   which is |V.firstVariation (fun y ↦ φ(|y − x|²/t²)•(y − x))| ≤ A·Λ·t·∫ φ(|y − x|²/t²) dμ_V(y). As all data were arbitrary, the statement holds.
